title: bug: wrapper attribution snapshot fingerprints a symlink by its target's content, not the link text git commits
description: The snapshot hash (scripts/moe-agent.sh ~2729 `hash-object --stdin-paths`, ps1 ~2460) follows symlinks, while `git add` stores the link text. So retargeting a link to a file with the same content reads as unchanged, and editing a link's target reads as the link changing. (Before task-b62c9fc7, every symlink candidate also dropped as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT.) Repro: `ln -s a l; git hash-object l` gives the hash of a's content, not of the string "a". Fix: hash symlinks by their readlink text (e.g. `printf %s "$(readlink p)" | git hash-object --stdin`) in both twins.
definitionOfDone: Both wrapper twins fingerprint a symlink by its link text in the baseline snapshot and the temp-index re-hash
Postflight cases in bash and ps1 cover a symlink retarget (lands) and an unchanged symlink (stays PREEXISTING)
